obligations.summary: Notified bodies must draw up certificates in a language easily understood by the relevant authorities in the Member State where the notified body is established.

Certificates issued by notified bodies must be valid for a period not exceeding five years for AI systems covered by Annex I and four years for AI systems covered by Annex III, with extensions available upon provider request based on re-assessment.
exceptions: At the provider's request, validity may be extended for further periods not exceeding five years (Annex I) or four years (Annex III) based on re-assessment.
Supplements to a certificate remain valid as long as the certificate they supplement is valid.

obligations.summary: Where a notified body finds that an AI system no longer meets the applicable requirements, it must, applying the principle of proportionality, suspend, withdraw, or impose restrictions on the certificate, unless the provider takes appropriate corrective action within a deadline set by the notified body.
exceptions: Suspension, withdrawal, or restriction may be avoided if the provider ensures compliance through appropriate corrective action within an appropriate deadline set by the notified body.
